newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Corp ups Israel Chemicals stake.
newsitem.headline: Israel Corp ups Israel Chemicals stake.

text.p: Israel Corp said on Tuesday it has acquired a further 12.45 percent of Israel Chemicals Ltd from Shoul Eisenberg for $128.4 million, doubling its holding.

To help finance the acquisition, Israel Corp said it would be selling Eisenberg, who has a controlling stake in Israel Corp, its 24.9 perecent interest in Eisen Oil China Corp (EOCC) for $32.9 million. EOCC has interests in 14 joint venture projects to produce edible oils in China.
The remaining $95.5 million will be financed by debt.

Israel Corp and Eisenberg together acquired a controlling 24.9 percent stake in Israel Chemicals from the Israeli government in February 1995 for $230.3 million. But the government prefers there be a single, domestic controlling shareholder.
The sale price reflected Israel Chemicals' average market capitalisation over the last 30 days on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

"The company sees the investment in Israel Chemicals as a long-term investment, and in order to produce the greatest benefits and continue preserving its right of management in Israel Chemicals, the company is interested in increasing its holding in Israel Chemicals by the purchase of additional shares," Israel Corp. said in a statement.
A plan in May 1995 to float 22 percent of the company failed, but at least part of the government's 50 percent holding in Israel Chemicals may be floated next year.

Newspaper reports this week said EOCC's other shareholders were disappointed with the company's performance, but today's sale by Israel Corp was apparently part of the conglomerate's strategy of consolidating its interests into core areas.
Israel Corp has holdings in Zim Israel Navigation, Israel Oil Refineries Ltd and Tower Semiconductor.
